rationale:
Split into 2 children.

Why. The supplied proof's Step 5 runs one estimate three times. Each error term E₁, E₂, E₃ is bounded by ‖f‖Rⁿ times the matching (P_i) density quotient at ρ = Rλ, and then sent to 0. This is Simon's upper-density estimate from the proof of 1.6 '⇒' (chapter-03.txt lines 127-140), in the weighted form of Remark 1.8(1). It is a genuine reusable obligation. Child blowup_error_vanishes (chartTD_blowup_integral_tendsto_zero) states it once, for an arbitrary set S and weight w: if w is integrable on S ∩ B_ρ(x) for every ρ > 0 and ρ^{-n}∫_{S∩B_ρ(x)} |w| → 0, then r^{-n}∫_S f(η_{x,r})·w → 0 for every f ∈ C_c. The glue uses it three times.
The rest of the proof's content is Steps 3-4: integrability, plus the exact splitting of ∫_M (f∘η_{x,r})θ along Γ (Simon's decomposition, lines 116-120, weighted). This is a separate measure-theoretic obligation. Child weighted_blowup_split (chartTD_weighted_blowup_integral_split) isolates it, stated on the unscaled side. Neither child therefore depends on the resolved uncle blowup_scaling (Submission.chartTD_setIntegral_blowUpMap_image), which only the parent glue uses. The two children are independent of each other, so they can be formalized in parallel. Neither restates the parent or solves another DAG node: the parent's sibling nodes (upper_density_zero, lebesgue_points, blowup_scaling) produce the hypotheses (P1)-(P3) and the scaling identity, and these children consume them.

How the children give the parent (the supplied proof's steps).
(1) finrank P = n is hT.1. Fix f ∈ C_c.
(2) E₁ → 0. Apply child A with (S, w) = (M∖Γ, θ). Hypothesis (i) holds because (M∖Γ) ∩ B_ρ(x) ⊆ M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and θ is integrable on M ∩ (compact closed ball). Hypothesis (ii) is (P1) verbatim.
(3) E₂ → 0. Apply child A with (Γ∖M, 1). (i) holds because Hⁿ((Γ∖M) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ Hⁿ(Γ) < ∞. (ii) is (P2), since ∫_{(Γ∖M)∩B_ρ(x)} |1| dHⁿ = Hⁿ((Γ∖M) ∩ B_ρ(x)).toReal (Measure.real).
(4) E₃ → 0. Apply child A with (M∩Γ, θ − θ(x)). (i) holds because θ is integrable on M ∩ B̄_ρ(x) and the constant is integrable on a set of finite measure. (ii) is (P3) verbatim.
(5) For r > 0, the uncle identity rewrites ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f(y)θ(x + ry) dHⁿ as r^{-n}∫_M f(η_{x,r}(z))θ(z), using x + r·η_{x,r}(z) = z. It also rewrites ∫_{η_{x,r}(Γ)} f as r^{-n}∫_Γ f∘η_{x,r}. Child B then gives the parent's Step 4 identity: I(r) = r^{-n}E₁' + θ(x)(∫_{η(Γ)} f − r^{-n}E₂') + r^{-n}E₃'.
(6) Def. 1.4 for Γ gives ∫_{η_{x,r}(Γ)} f → ∫_P f. Together with (2)-(4), I(r) → θ(x)∫_P f, which is Def. 1.7.

theorem Submission.chartTD_weighted_tangent_of_density : (∀ (n N : ℕ) (M Γ : Set (Rn N)) (θ : Rn N → ℝ) (x : Rn N) (P : Submodule ℝ (Rn N)), NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n] → NullMeasurableSet Γ μHE[n] → μHE[n] Γ < ∞ → IsPositiveLocallyIntegrableWeight n M θ → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n Γ x P → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ (ρ ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ z in (M \ Γ) ∩ Metric.ball x ρ, |θ z| ∂μHE[n]) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ (ρ ^ n)⁻¹ * (μHE[n] ((Γ \ M) ∩ Metric.ball x ρ)).toReal) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ (ρ ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ z in M ∩ Γ ∩ Metric.ball x ρ, |θ z - θ x| ∂μHE[n]) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M θ x P) := by
  intro n N M Γ θ x P hM hΓ hΓfin hθ hT hP1 hP2 hP3
  refine ⟨hT.1, fun f => ?_⟩
  have hθloc : ∀ ρ : ℝ, IntegrableOn θ (M ∩ Metric.closedBall x ρ) μHE[n] :=
    fun ρ => hθ.2.2 _ (isCompact_closedBall x ρ)
  have hfin : ∀ T ⊆ Γ, (μHE[n] : Measure (Rn N)) T ≠ ∞ :=
    fun T hT => ((measure_mono hT).trans_lt hΓfin).ne
  -- (E₁) the part of `M` off `Γ`
  have hE1 := Submission.chartTD_blowup_integral_tendsto_zero n N (M \ Γ) θ x
    (fun ρ _ => (hθloc ρ).mono_set
      (fun z hz => ⟨hz.1.1, Metric.ball_subset_closedBall hz.2⟩)) hP1 f
  -- (E₂) the part of `Γ` off `M`
  have hE2 := Submission.chartTD_blowup_integral_tendsto_zero n N (Γ \ M) (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) x
    (fun ρ _ => integrableOn_const (hfin _ (fun z hz => hz.1.1)))
    (hP2.congr (fun ρ => by simp [Measure.real])) f
  -- (E₃) the oscillation of `θ` on `M ∩ Γ`
  have hE3 := Submission.chartTD_blowup_integral_tendsto_zero n N (M ∩ Γ) (fun z => θ z - θ x) x
    (fun ρ _ => ((hθloc ρ).mono_set
      (fun z hz => ⟨hz.1.1, Metric.ball_subset_closedBall hz.2⟩)).sub
        (integrableOn_const (hfin _ (fun z hz => hz.1.2)))) hP3 f
  have hG := hT.2 f

      θ x * (∫ y in blowUpMap x r '' Γ, f y ∂μHE[n] -
        (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ z in Γ \ M, f (blowUpMap x r z) * (fun _ => (1 : ℝ)) z ∂μHE[n]) +
      (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ z in M ∩ Γ, f (blowUpMap x r z) * (fun z => θ z - θ x) z ∂μHE[n])
      =ᶠ[𝓝[>] 0] (fun r : ℝ ↦ ∫ y in blowUpMap x r '' M, f y * θ (x + r • y) ∂μHE[n]) := by
    filter_upwards [self_mem_nhdsWithin] with r hr
    have hr0 : (0 : ℝ) < r := hr
    have hxz : ∀ z : Rn N, x + r • blowUpMap x r z = z := by
      intro z; simp [blowUpMap, smul_smul, hr0.ne']
    rw [Submission.chartTD_setIntegral_blowUpMap_image N n x r hr0 M,
      Submission.chartTD_setIntegral_blowUpMap_image N n x r hr0 Γ]
    simp only [hxz, mul_one]
    rw [Submission.chartTD_weighted_blowup_integral_split n N M Γ θ x f r hr0 hM hΓ hΓfin hθ]
    ring
  refine Tendsto.congr' heq ?_
  have hlim := (hE1.add ((tendsto_const_nhds (x := θ x)).mul (hG.sub hE2))).add hE3

subproblems.title: Vanishing normalized density of |w| on S forces the normalized blow-up integrals of f·w over S to vanish (Simon's upper-density estimate in the proof of 1.6 '⇒'; parent Step 5)
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, let S ⊆ ℝ^N be an arbitrary set, w : ℝ^N → ℝ a function and x ∈ ℝ^N; write η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r) and Hⁿ = μHE[n], with ∫_T h dHⁿ the Bochner integral against the restriction Hⁿ⌞T (T need not be measurable; non-integrable functions have integral 0). Assume (i) w is Hⁿ-integrable on S ∩ B_ρ(x) for every ρ > 0, where B_ρ(x) = Metric.ball x ρ is the open ball, and (ii) ρ^{-n}∫_{S∩B_ρ(x)} |w| dHⁿ → 0 as ρ ↓ 0 (ρ^{-n} is Lean's (ρ ^ n)⁻¹; ↓ 0 is the filter 𝓝[>] 0). Then for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), r^{-n}∫_S f(η_{x,r}(z))·w(z) dHⁿ(z) → 0 as r ↓ 0.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (S : Set (Rn N)) (w : Rn N → ℝ) (x : Rn N), (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → IntegrableOn w (S ∩ Metric.ball x ρ) μHE[n]) → Tendsto (fun ρ : ℝ ↦ (ρ ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ z in S ∩ Metric.ball x ρ, |w z| ∂μHE[n]) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0) → ∀ f : C_c(Rn N, ℝ), Tendsto (fun r : ℝ ↦ (r ^ n)⁻¹ * ∫ z in S, f (blowUpMap x r z) * w z ∂μHE[n]) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. This is the upper-density estimate of Simon's proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' (chapter-03.txt lines 127-140: |∫_{η_{x,λ}(M∖N_j)} f dHⁿ| ≤ sup|f|·Hⁿ(B_R(0) ∩ η_{x,λ}(M∖N_j)) = sup|f|·λ^{-n}Hⁿ(B_{λR}(x) ∩ M∖N_j) → 0), written on the unscaled side and with a weight w as in Remark 1.8(1) (lines 298-306). It is the bound of Step 5 of the parent proof (|E_i(λ)| ≤ ‖f‖Rⁿ·(the (P_i) quotient at ρ = Rλ)), extracted as one lemma that the parent applies three times. Conventions: η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r); Hⁿ = μHE[n]; ∫_T h dHⁿ is the Bochner integral of h against the restriction Hⁿ⌞T (T need not be measurable; the integral of a non-integrable function is 0).

1. Constants from f. f is continuous with compact support, so there is C with |f(y)| ≤ C for all y (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support); C ≥ |f(0)| ≥ 0. The topological support tsupport f is compact, hence bounded, so tsupport f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0) for some R₀ (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball). Put R := max(R₀, 1), so R > 0. If f(y) ≠ 0 then y ∈ tsupport f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0), so ‖y‖ < R₀ ≤ R.

2. Localization, for fixed r > 0. Let z ∈ ℝ^N with f(η_{x,r}(z)) ≠ 0. By step 1, r⁻¹‖z − x‖ = ‖η_{x,r}(z)‖ < R, hence ‖z − x‖ < Rr, i.e. z ∈ B_{Rr}(x). Put b_r(z) := 1_{B_{Rr}(x)}(z)·C|w(z)|. Then |f(η_{x,r}(z))·w(z)| ≤ b_r(z) for every z ∈ ℝ^N. If f(η_{x,r}(z)) = 0, the left side is 0 ≤ b_r(z), because C ≥ 0. Otherwise z ∈ B_{Rr}(x), so b_r(z) = C|w(z)|, and |f(η_{x,r}(z))| ≤ C.

3. Integrability of the majorant. Since Rr > 0, hypothesis (i) gives that w, and hence C|w|, is Hⁿ-integrable on S ∩ B_{Rr}(x). The open ball B_{Rr}(x) is a Borel set. So b_r is integrable with respect to Hⁿ⌞S iff C|w| is integrable with respect to (Hⁿ⌞S)⌞B_{Rr}(x) = Hⁿ⌞(S ∩ B_{Rr}(x)) (integrable_indicator_iff, Measure.restrict_restrict). Hence b_r is Hⁿ⌞S-integrable.

4. Estimate. For Bochner integrals, |∫ F dμ| ≤ ∫ G dμ whenever G is μ-integrable and |F| ≤ G μ-a.e. (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le). No measurability of F is needed: if F is not μ-integrable, the left side is 0 ≤ ∫ G dμ, since G ≥ 0. Apply this with μ = Hⁿ⌞S, F(z) = f(η_{x,r}(z))·w(z) and G = b_r (steps 2 and 3). Then use ∫_S 1_{B_{Rr}(x)}·C|w| dHⁿ = C·∫_{S∩B_{Rr}(x)} |w| dHⁿ (setIntegral_indicator for the Borel set B_{Rr}(x), integral_const_mul). This gives
 |∫_S f(η_{x,r}(z))·w(z) dHⁿ(z)| ≤ C·∫_{S∩B_{Rr}(x)} |w| dHⁿ.
 Multiply by r^{-n} > 0 and use r^{-n} = Rⁿ·(Rr)^{-n}:
 |r^{-n}∫_S f(η_{x,r}(z))·w(z) dHⁿ(z)| ≤ C·Rⁿ·Q(Rr), where Q(ρ) := ρ^{-n}∫_{S∩B_ρ(x)} |w| dHⁿ.
 This holds for every r > 0.

5. Limit. The map r ↦ Rr tends to 0 as r → 0 and is positive for r > 0, so it maps the filter 𝓝[>]0 into 𝓝[>]0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_of_tendsto_nhds_of_eventually_within). By hypothesis (ii), Q(ρ) → 0 as ρ ↓ 0. Composing, Q(Rr) → 0 as r ↓ 0, and so C·Rⁿ·Q(Rr) → 0. The bound of step 4 holds for all r > 0, that is, eventually along 𝓝[>]0. The squeeze principle (squeeze_zero_norm') therefore gives r^{-n}∫_S f(η_{x,r}(z))·w(z) dHⁿ(z) → 0 as r ↓ 0, which is the claim.

6. Remarks. No measurability of S, and none of w beyond hypothesis (i), is used. For n = 0, r^{-n} = Rⁿ = 1 and the argument is unchanged. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose C ≥ 0 with |f| ≤ C and R > 0 with f(y) ≠ 0 ⇒ ‖y‖ < R (compact support).
For r > 0: f(η_{x,r}(z)) ≠ 0 ⇒ z ∈ B_{Rr}(x), so |f(η_{x,r}(z))w(z)| ≤ 1_{B_{Rr}(x)}(z)·C|w(z)| for all z.
The majorant is Hⁿ⌞S-integrable by hypothesis (i) at ρ = Rr (Borel ball, restrict_restrict).
r ↦ Rr maps 𝓝[>]0 to 𝓝[>]0, so the bound → 0 by (ii); squeeze gives the limit 0.

subproblems.title: Exact splitting of the localized weighted integral ∫_M (f∘η_{x,r})θ along a comparison set Γ (Simon's decomposition in the proof of 1.6 '⇒', weighted; parent Steps 3-4)
subproblems.statement: Let n, N ∈ ℕ, let M, Γ ⊆ ℝ^N be Hⁿ-null-measurable (Hⁿ = μHE[n]) with Hⁿ(Γ) < ∞, let θ be a positive locally integrable weight on M (IsPositiveLocallyIntegrableWeight n M θ: θ > 0 on M, θ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e.-measurable, θ ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ K)) for every compact K), let x ∈ ℝ^N, f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), r > 0, and put g(z) := f(η_{x,r}(z)) with η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r). Then, with Bochner integrals against the restricted measures, ∫_M g θ dHⁿ = ∫_{M∖Γ} g θ dHⁿ + θ(x)·(∫_Γ g dHⁿ − ∫_{Γ∖M} g dHⁿ) + ∫_{M∩Γ} g·(θ − θ(x)) dHⁿ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (n N : ℕ) (M Γ : Set (Rn N)) (θ : Rn N → ℝ) (x : Rn N) (f : C_c(Rn N, ℝ)) (r : ℝ), 0 < r → NullMeasurableSet M μHE[n] → NullMeasurableSet Γ μHE[n] → μHE[n] Γ < ∞ → IsPositiveLocallyIntegrableWeight n M θ → ∫ z in M, f (blowUpMap x r z) * θ z ∂μHE[n] = ∫ z in M \ Γ, f (blowUpMap x r z) * θ z ∂μHE[n] + θ x * (∫ z in Γ, f (blowUpMap x r z) ∂μHE[n] - ∫ z in Γ \ M, f (blowUpMap x r z) ∂μHE[n]) + ∫ z in M ∩ Γ, f (blowUpMap x r z) * (θ z - θ x) ∂μHE[n]
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source. Steps 3-4 of the parent proof. This is the decomposition in Simon's proof of Theorem 1.6 '⇒' (chapter-03.txt lines 116-120: ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N_j)} f dHⁿ − ∫_{η_{x,λ}(N_j∖M_j)} f dHⁿ + ∫_{η_{x,λ}(M∖M_j)} f dHⁿ), in the weighted form of Definition 1.7 and Remark 1.8(1) (lines 284-306). It is written on the unscaled side, before the change of variables, and on M ∩ Γ the weight is split as θ = θ(x) + (θ − θ(x)). Conventions: η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x) (SimonGMT blowUpMap x r); Hⁿ = μHE[n]; ∫_T h dHⁿ is the Bochner integral against Hⁿ⌞T; g(z) := f(η_{x,r}(z)).

1. Properties of g. Since f ∈ C_c(ℝ^N, ℝ), there is C with |f(y)| ≤ C for all y, so C ≥ 0 (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support). There is also R₀ with tsupport f ⊆ B_{R₀}(0) (compact, hence bounded: Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball), so f(y) ≠ 0 ⇒ ‖y‖ < R₀. The map η_{x,r} is affine, hence continuous, so g is continuous and |g| ≤ C. If g(z) ≠ 0, then r⁻¹‖z − x‖ = ‖η_{x,r}(z)‖ < R₀. Since r > 0, ‖z − x‖ < R₀r, so z ∈ K := B̄_{R₀r}(x).

2. gθ is Hⁿ-integrable on M. K is a closed ball in ℝ^N, hence compact and Borel. So θ is Hⁿ-integrable on M ∩ K by the third clause of IsPositiveLocallyIntegrableWeight n M θ.
 Measurability: g is continuous, hence strongly measurable, and θ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. measurable by the second clause. So gθ is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable.
 Domination: |g(z)θ(z)| ≤ 1_K(z)·C|θ(z)| for every z. If g(z) = 0 the left side is 0; otherwise z ∈ K by step 1 and |g(z)| ≤ C.
 The majorant 1_K·C|θ| is Hⁿ⌞M-integrable, because K is Borel and C|θ| is integrable on M ∩ K (integrable_indicator_iff, Measure.restrict_restrict). By domination (Integrable.mono'), gθ is integrable on M.

3. g is Hⁿ-integrable on Γ. Hⁿ⌞Γ is a finite measure because Hⁿ(Γ) < ∞. The function g is continuous, hence strongly measurable, and bounded by C. A bounded, strongly measurable function is integrable for a finite measure (Integrable.of_bound).

4. Integrability on M ∩ Γ. By restriction (IntegrableOn.mono_set), gθ is integrable on M ∩ Γ ⊆ M (step 2), and g is integrable on M ∩ Γ ⊆ Γ (step 3). Hence g·(θ − θ(x)), which equals gθ − θ(x)·g pointwise, is integrable on M ∩ Γ.

5. Three exact identities. If t is Hⁿ-null-measurable and F is Hⁿ-integrable on s, then ∫_{s∩t} F + ∫_{s∖t} F = ∫_s F (integral_inter_add_sdiff₀).
 (a) Take s = M, t = Γ (null-measurable by hypothesis) and F = gθ (step 2): ∫_M gθ = ∫_{M∩Γ} gθ + ∫_{M∖Γ} gθ.
 (b) Take s = Γ, t = M (null-measurable by hypothesis) and F = g (step 3): ∫_Γ g = ∫_{Γ∩M} g + ∫_{Γ∖M} g, and Γ ∩ M = M ∩ Γ.
 (c) On M ∩ Γ, gθ = θ(x)·g + g·(θ − θ(x)) pointwise, and both terms are integrable there (step 4). By additivity and homogeneity of the integral (integral_add, integral_const_mul), ∫_{M∩Γ} gθ = θ(x)·∫_{M∩Γ} g + ∫_{M∩Γ} g·(θ − θ(x)).

6. Conclusion. From (a) and (c),
 ∫_M gθ = θ(x)·∫_{M∩Γ} g + ∫_{M∩Γ} g·(θ − θ(x)) + ∫_{M∖Γ} gθ.
